solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Knock off sides of discharge tube

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two end letters, here those of discharge

parts.note: a duct is a tube or channel carrying fluid

explanation.surface: Instructions to strip the outer casing off a discharge tube, like a fluorescent lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock off a sum from a price is to subtract it, the same as taking it away.

clue.text: One runs odd parts of Tube through Embankment, which takes one off roads?

indicators.note: through means the pieces pass into the middle of the word around them

parts.note: a dike is an embankment or dyke
I is the Roman numeral for one
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: odd parts are the first, third and so on letters of Tube

explanation.surface: A commuter traces the Tube along London's Embankment, then a vehicle that leaves the roads.
explanation.walkthrough: The Embankment is a road along the Thames in London, and an Underground station; here it is DIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirt bike is a motorcycle built for off-road riding, carrying its rider away from tarmac.

clue.text: Done in, is Dad looking down and feeling better?

indicators.note: done means cooked or worked over, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Father, exhausted, is looking low and recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done in' reads as exhausted, but 'Done' alone is the anagram signal and 'in' joins the fodder. The definition reads 'looking down' as looking down on others.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is contempt, scorn for those one regards as beneath oneself, a sense of superiority.

clue.text: French jeweller almost overcomes delay to make stuff found in ears

indicators.note: overcomes is read as coming over and around, so the word encloses the delay
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Cartier is the famous French jewellery house
lag is a delay

explanation.surface: A Paris jeweller nearly overcomes a hold-up to make earrings.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer ear is shaped by flexible cartilage, the tissue you feel in the ear flap.

clue.text: Sensitive spot, roughly abused, time and time again

indicators.note: roughly suggests rough handling, so the letters are knocked about into a new order
time and time again says the time letter appears twice over

explanation.surface: Someone describes a sore point that has been mistreated over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges ABUSED together with the two Ts from 'time and time again'; the Ts land inside the result, so they belong in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste bud is a small receptor on the tongue, a tiny sensitive spot for flavour.

clue.text: Rashly say 'Macbeth' with ease according to circumstances

indicators.note: rashly suggests acting carelessly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor carelessly says 'Macbeth' in a theatre, a famous taboo, quite casually.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'with' joins the two parts of the fodder. Saying 'Macbeth' in a theatre is held to be bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: This set phrase means depending on how things turn out, whichever applies.

clue.text: Groan, perhaps, as persistent ringing's not got hold of pub

indicators.note: not got hold of means a piece is missing from the word

parts.note: tinnitus is a persistent ringing in the ears; the 's stands for has
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A sufferer's groan as the constant ringing in the ears won't let go of the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groan' is not a moan: Titus Groan is the hero of Mervyn Peake's Gormenghast novels, so 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus is the first name of Titus Groan, title character of Peake's novel, so one Groan is so called.

clue.text: Island with special quality requisitioned by Crown

indicators.note: requisitioned by means taken into the other word, held inside it

parts.note: the crown of the head holds the brain, and crown is slang for head
it is that indefinable special quality, as in 'she has it'

explanation.surface: An island's special character is commandeered by the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Britain is the largest island of the British Isles.

clue.text: Type of game involving king, king who had success with Israelites

indicators.note: involving means the word wraps around the pieces

parts.note: deer are hunted as game
K is the chess abbreviation for king
K again for the second king

explanation.surface: A board game featuring two kings and a biblical king who led the Israelites to victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Israelites' suggests the Bible, but it is a 1969 ska hit by Desmond Dekker.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaican singer Desmond Dekker topped the UK charts with the song Israelites.

clue.text: Representative in Strasbourg, the man's best man, mostly minor person with soul-destroying job?

parts.note: an MEP, Member of the European Parliament, sits in Strasbourg
his means belonging to the man
top means best
he refers to a man

indicators.note: mostly means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: less means minor or lesser

explanation.surface: An MEP's best man, nearly a junior figure, does a soul-crushing job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soul-destroying' reads as tedious work but means literally taking souls: Mephistopheles is the devil who buys Faust's soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephistopheles is the demon of the Faust legend, who claims souls for hell in exchange for favours.

clue.text: At first, the crew mistake employer's backing for raise

indicators.note: backing means everything built so far is read from right to left
at first asks for the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
a user is one who employs something; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A crew blunders first, and the boss's backing is sought for a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the whole string round, not just the employer. 'raise' is the verb, as in raising the dead, not a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To resurrect something is to bring it back to life, to raise it from the dead.

clue.text: Hold narrow edge of knife

parts.note: thin means narrow or slender

indicators.note: the edge of a word is its first letter, here from knife

explanation.surface: An instruction to grip a knife by its fine cutting edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' is a verb of opinion, as in 'I hold that...', not a grip.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold a view is to believe or consider it true, the sense of thinking so.

clue.text: Suffer current silence with a gruff attitude?

parts.note: to bear something is to suffer or endure it
I is the physics symbol for electric current
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with an ongoing silence while in a grumpy mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearish means rough and surly in manner, behaving like a grumpy bear.

clue.text: Some retrospective retrieval's needing force to work

indicators.note: retrospective says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A looking-back analysis says some retrieval needs to be forced into action.
explanation.definitionFit: To enslave people is to make slaves of them, compelling them to labour without choice.

clue.text: Important area including northern equatorial region

indicators.note: including means the first pieces hold the next one inside them

parts.note: key means important or crucial

explanation.surface: A key region near the equator is said to take in a northern zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya is an East African country straddling the equator, so it is a region on that line.

clue.text: Rocky performances made him put a person off

parts.note: with off, which follows the person, put off means stall, to delay someone
one means a person, as in 'one does one's best'

explanation.surface: Shaky performances led to someone getting the brush-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... off' is STALL and 'a person' is ONE. 'Rocky' is the boxing film series, not unsteady acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvester Stallone found stardom playing the boxer in the Rocky films, which made his career.

clue.text: Profligate Wooster, possibly deficient in occupation

indicators.note: in means the shortened name sits inside the other word

parts.note: a line is a line of work, an occupation

indicators.note: deficient means lacking its last letter

parts.note: Bertie Wooster is P G Wodehouse's comic hero; possibly marks the name as an example

explanation.surface: Bertie Wooster, the idle wastrel, may well be short of a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertine is a dissolute person given to unrestrained pleasure, a wastrel.

clue.text: Yarn's cut on something below jack in loom

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: a thread is a yarn; the 's stands for is
in a suit of cards the ten ranks just below the jack

explanation.surface: A weaver's yarn is cut by something beneath a jack in the loom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loom' looks like the weaving frame, as yarn and jack suggest; it is the verb, to hang over menacingly. 'on' places TEN after.
explanation.definitionFit: When danger looms it hangs over people threateningly, appearing imminent.

clue.text: Trap a king: what stops merry old one?

indicators.note: stops means the pieces plug the gap inside another word, like a stopper

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme was a merry old soul
K is the chess abbreviation for king
eh? is an exclamation meaning 'what?'

explanation.surface: Someone schemes to ensnare a monarch and wonders what will stop the jolly old fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' is British slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'; CAKEHOLE is another slang word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal British slang for the mouth, the opening a cheeky person shuts.

clue.text: Scottish island accepts raised American regular charge

indicators.note: accepts means the island takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a GI is a regular American soldier

explanation.surface: A Scottish island takes on a promoted American soldier at regular cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call someone before a court to answer an accusation.

clue.text: Discharge law primarily displacing number of judges

indicators.note: displacing means one letter pushes out another and takes its place

parts.note: the bench is the collective name for judges

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of law

explanation.surface: A legal ruling might discharge or displace a group of judges.
explanation.definitionFit: To belch is to expel wind from the stomach noisily, a discharge of gas.

clue.text: Splitting stage, also known as energy containment failure

indicators.note: splitting means the piece breaks into the other word

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A reactor stage splits, a nuclear accident also known as a containment failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A leakage is an escape of fluid or gas, a failure to keep it contained.

clue.text: Quote the writer's brought up, leading to upbringing?

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote
me refers to the writer; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A writer quotes their own upbringing as formative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upbringing' here means bringing up food, vomiting; 'brought up' is a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic causes vomiting, so it literally leads to bringing up one's stomach contents.

clue.text: Man in the news a lot, implicating third of Tory party?

indicators.note: implicating is read as folding something within, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: much means a lot

indicators.note: third of asks for the third letter of Tory

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A man often in the headlines, implicated in a Conservative party scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Murdoch owns News Corp, so he is literally a man in the news business.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Murdoch is a newspaper proprietor, both owning news outlets and often featured in them.

clue.text: Eccentric selection of accoutrements

indicators.note: a selection of says a run of consecutive letters is picked from inside the word

explanation.surface: A quirky choice of accessories.
explanation.definitionFit: Outre is a French borrowing for unconventional or bizarre, so it describes eccentric behaviour.

clue.text: Head off bombardment, smothering one's aggression in high places

indicators.note: smothering means the word wraps around and covers another piece
head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a barrage is a heavy bombardment of artillery fire
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone tries to forestall an attack while suppressing rage among the powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Air rage is violent behaviour by passengers on a flight, aggression literally high in the sky.

clue.text: Chump steak initially is bound by twine

indicators.note: is bound by means the letter is enclosed by the word around it

parts.note: a twit is a chump or fool

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of steak

explanation.surface: A cut of chump steak is first tied up with string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chump' looks like part of 'chump steak', a British cut of lamb; it is TWIT. 'twine' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine strands is to wind or coil them together, the sense of twisting.

clue.text: Vigorously rub in talc, overcoming friction

indicators.note: vigorously suggests energetic action, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to work talcum powder firmly into the skin to stop chafing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the adjective here: lubricant means serving to reduce friction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lubricant makes surfaces slippery, so it works against rubbing and resistance.

clue.text: Hollows in volcanic height become thicker

indicators.note: in means the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: a cone is the peak built up by a volcano
dens are hollows or lairs

explanation.surface: Hollows in a volcano's summit grow denser.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense is to grow denser or more concentrated, as vapour turns to liquid.

clue.text: Disconnect new home of renowned bore

parts.note: to sever is to cut off or disconnect

explanation.surface: Someone cuts ties with the new house of a famously dull person.
explanation.walkthrough: The bore is not a tedious person: the Severn, Britain's longest river, has a famous tidal wave called the Severn Bore.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn Bore is a large tidal surge running up the river's estuary, so the river hosts it.
